newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks rally with Dow, U.S. Fed decision.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks rally with Dow, U.S. Fed decision.

text.p: Mexican stocks soared to end above the key 5,000-point mark on Tuesday, breaking six days of losses as bargain-hunters returned in the wake of gains on Wall Street after the U.S. Federal Reserve left U.S. interest rates unchanged.
"The fact U.S. rates did not change is what is bolstering the market," said Jose Gomez, an analyst at the Value brokerage.
The Fed at its policy-setting meeting on Tuesday opted to keep interest rates steady amid overwhelming evidence the world's most powerful economy is growing solidly while inflation is low.
The blue-chip IPC share index soared 88.60 points, or 1.79 percent, at 5,041.48.
The Dow Jones industrial average meanwhile climbed 114.74 points to close at 7,918.10.
Gomez said investor confidence had gradually returned to the bourse after the recent slew of losses had made prices ripe for bargain hunters.
"The fact that prices fell so sharply made them attractive, especially for short-term investors. The market is recouping lost ground and we can see that in improving volume," he said.
On the broad market, gainers trounced losers by 70 to 25, out of 119 stocks traded in total. Volume was moderate at 96.8 million shares but much heavier than Monday's dismal total.

Market heavyweight Telefonos de Mexico set the pace, dealers said, gaining 20 centavos (2.5 cents) to 20.40 pesos ($2.63). The telecommunications firm's American Depositary Receipts meanwhile ended up 15/16 at 52-1/2.
Traders said financial groups gained sharply after the FOMC decision as investors looked forward to lower interest rates at home and a consequent improvement in loan quality.
Bancomer, one of Mexico's biggest financial groups, ended up 22 centavos (3 cent) at 5.46 pesos (70 cents).
Glassmaker Vitro was a prominent gainer, rising 1.40 pesos (18 cents) to 36.40 ($4.69) on Monday's late news it had formed a $100 million joint venture with Libbey Inc., dealers said.

Television network TV Azteca fell 1.37 pesos (18 cents) to 35.43 ($4.56), the price at which it went public on Friday, while its rival Televisa gained 4.00 pesos (51 cents) to 127.00 ($16.36) on news it would issue $1.6 billion in commercial paper, dealers said.
